name: Aceclofenac
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Aceclofenac is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) partly converted to diclofenac; about two-thirds of a dose leaves in urine as metabolites. NSAIDs can precipitate kidney failure in at-risk patients. The European label needs no dose change in mild kidney impairment (with caution), asks for the lowest dose and regular kidney monitoring in mild to moderate impairment, and contraindicates it in severe impairment. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The SmPC grades kidney impairment as mild, moderate or severe without numbers; bands map 'severe' to creatinine clearance (CrCl) <30 mL/min.

bands.recommendation: Usual: 100 mg twice daily; maximum 200 mg/day (SmPC). Mild impairment: no dose change but caution.

Mild to moderate impairment: lowest effective dose with surveillance and regular kidney function checks (SmPC). Avoid with volume depletion or diuretics where possible. Short courses only; hold during intercurrent illness or volume depletion (sick-day rule; KDIGO 2024).
Severe kidney impairment: contraindicated (SmPC; no numeric threshold). Our mapping of 'severe' to CrCl <30 is a judgment.
Severe kidney impairment: contraindicated (SmPC; no numeric threshold). Our mapping of 'severe' to CrCl <30 is a judgment.

pd.text: Contraindicated (severe kidney impairment; SmPC). NSAIDs hasten loss of residual kidney function.

crrt.text: Contraindicated; NSAIDs worsen acute kidney injury.

monitoring: Kidney function regularly in mild to moderate impairment, heart failure, liver disease, diuretic use, after major surgery and in older adults; blood pressure; potassium with potassium-sparing diuretics; gastrointestinal bleeding (SmPC 4.4). Check creatinine and potassium within 1–2 weeks of starting in CKD or with an ACE inhibitor, ARB, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) or diuretic; avoid the NSAID + ACE inhibitor/ARB + diuretic ("triple whammy") combination and long-term use in CKD.

pediatric.approved_ages: Not established in children and adolescents (SmPC).
